claims.text: Controlled aging of a homogenized HEA induces nanoscale coherent precipitates.
The precipitates can be distributed uniformly within the HEA matrix.
Aging-induced coherent precipitates increase yield strength relative to a solution-annealed homogeneous microstructure.
Aging-induced coherent precipitates increase ductility relative to a solution-annealed homogeneous microstructure.
Aging-induced coherent precipitates increase Young's modulus relative to a solution-annealed homogeneous microstructure.
Aging-induced coherent precipitates increase fracture resistance relative to a solution-annealed homogeneous microstructure.
Nanoscale precipitates pin dislocations and thereby produce precipitation hardening.
Nanoscale coherent precipitates promote more uniform plastic deformation.
Nanoscale coherent precipitates reduce strain localization.
More uniform deformation and reduced strain localization enhance ductility and fracture resistance.
A precipitate dispersion can modify effective Young's modulus by changing the local bonding environment and load-transfer characteristics.
The proposed mechanism applies only to HEA compositions capable of forming coherent precipitates at accessible aging temperatures.
Precipitate coarsening or loss of coherence is expected to prevent the proposed simultaneous property improvements.
The magnitudes of the property changes depend on alloy system and aging parameters.
Failure to obtain statistically significant simultaneous improvements in all four targeted properties relative to an identical solution-annealed control would falsify the hypothesis.
